results.input: Aria Voss is trapped in the Ice Citadel. Suggest an escape that uses fire magic.
results.answer:
Aria has flint, 20 mana, and a broken sword. She can cast fire magic because she carries the flint [d40003b6].

Here are three escape options:

1. Cast fire magic to melt ice barriers or the lock on a door. A minor fire spell costs 5-15 mana [eac3e3c8], so she has enough. She could burn through ice or heat metal to open an exit—but the lore does not describe which barriers exist or what they are made of, so this depends on the Citadel's layout.

2. Use her flint and broken sword as a conventional fire: strike them together to start an ordinary (non-magical) fire [d40003b6]. Ordinary fire burns normally in the Citadel, even without magic, so she could use it to melt ice or burn through wood. But again, this works only if the exit is made of material that fire can destroy.

3. Wait for the Night of Thaw (the last night of Long Winter). During that night, the eastern wall loses its ward and can be crossed [c8557954]. Fire magic is still restricted even then, but she could potentially flee through the Eastern Postern if she can avoid the doubled guard.

Which approach fits your story?
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Aria Voss is at Ice Citadel, condition healthy, mana 20, health 85, carries: flint, broken sword, health potion

[search_lore] passage eac3e3c8 (The Magic of Aethel > The Three Disciplines): There are three disciplines of magic. Fire, also called pyromancy, creates and shapes flame and heat. Frost, also called cryomancy, creates and shapes ice and cold. Aether covers everything that works on distance and boundaries: teleportation, wards and scrying.

A minor spell of any discipline costs between 5 and 15 mana. A fire bolt costs 12 mana and a frost lance costs 15 mana. Greater workings, such as summoning a storm, cost far more and are limited to Archmages.
[search_lore] passage d40003b6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Fire magic and the Ice Citadel): Fire magic cannot be cast inside the Ice Citadel unless the caster possesses flint. The walls of the Citadel are woven with the Frost Binding, an old working that smothers every spell of the Fire discipline the moment it is cast. Flint is the single exception, because a flint holds a stolen spark that the Frost Binding recognises and lets pass.

Possession means carrying the flint on one's person. It does not have to be struck, held in the hand or shown to anyone. A caster with a flint in a pocket can cast fire magic anywhere inside the Citadel.

The ban applies to magic only. Torches, candles, forge fires and the Great Hearth burn normally inside the Citadel, because ordinary fire is not a spell.
[search_lore] passage 8f22b8dd (The Ice Citadel > The Visitor's Primer): The Wardens give every visitor a short booklet called the Visitor's Primer. It lists the rules of the Citadel in plain words. It says that a visitor who wishes to cast fire magic must strike their flint on the steel before every casting, and that an unstruck flint is not enough.

This instruction does not agree with the law of magic recorded in the Archive of the Glass Library, which says that carrying the flint is enough. Visitors who have followed the Primer and struck their flint have never been refused, so nobody has tested which rule is right.

[search_lore] passage f34602a1 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > How the wards work): The four walls of the Citadel are protected by wards that were raised after the founding of the fortress. They stop teleportation and scrying. Only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens, and only for one hour at a time.
[search_lore] passage 1fe24429 (The Ice Citadel > Layout > The four walls): The Citadel has four walls: north, south, east and west. All four are warded. A warded wall cannot be crossed by teleportation, in either direction, so nobody can teleport into the Citadel or out of it. The western wall holds the Gate of Frost, which is the main entrance. The eastern wall holds a small door called the Eastern Postern, which is kept barred and guarded all year.
[search_lore] passage c8557954 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > The Night of Thaw): Once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall of the Citadel is unwarded. The ward on the eastern wall goes down at midnight and comes back up at dawn. The Wardens say that the ice must be allowed to breathe while the Frost Binding renews itself.

During the Night of Thaw the eastern wall can be crossed by teleportation like any open ground, and the guard on the Eastern Postern is doubled. The other three walls stay warded. The Frost Binding that smothers fire magic stays in force all night, so fire magic is still impossible inside the Citadel on the Night of Thaw unless the caster possesses flint.

judge.reasoning: The answer claims Aria carries flint, has 20 mana and a broken sword, and can cast because she carries the flint; all of this is supported. A minor spell costing 5-15 mana is supported. Ordinary fire burns normally, which is supported, but striking the flint on the broken sword to make fire is general knowledge and not in the lore. That is a small extension. For option 3, the evidence says the wall can be crossed by teleportation and the Postern guard is doubled. The answer's 'flee through the Eastern Postern' implies a physical route, but the Postern is barred and the lore never says the unwarding opens it. It also says fire magic is 'still restricted' without noting that her flint exempts her. These are mild unsupported claims about the story. Constraint 1: the answer never says fire magic is normally smothered in the Citadel; it only says she can cast because of the flint. Fail. Constraint 2: no spell over 20 mana is suggested. Pass.

results.input: Aria Voss needs to leave the Ice Citadel at once. Have her teleport out and describe how.
results.answer:
Aria cannot teleport out of the Ice Citadel right now. All four walls are warded against teleportation in both directions [1fe24429]. The only exception is the eastern wall during the Night of Thaw, the last night of the Long Winter, when the ward drops from midnight to dawn [c8557954].

Aria has 20 mana and carries flint, a broken sword, and a health potion. To leave at once without waiting for the Night of Thaw, she would need to use the physical exits: the Gate of Frost (main entrance, west wall) or the Eastern Postern (east wall, guarded). This requires a change to the story, as teleportation is blocked by the wards.

results.input: Sera Quill wants to open the Restricted Stacks of the Glass Library to read the blood-casting treatises. How can she get in?
results.answer:
According to the official records, Sera holds no silver key and has never entered the Restricted Stacks [59e8ea2e]. However, there is a rumour that she has read the blood-casting treatises there, which she has neither confirmed nor denied, and the Head Archivist has declined to comment [59e8ea2e].

To open the Restricted Stacks legitimately, Sera would need to obtain one of the three silver keys from the key holders: the Head Archivist, the Deputy Archivist, or the Keeper of the Concord [d5a7cf5b]. This would require negotiating with one of them, likely by requesting access on scholarly grounds.

The Head Archivist holds one, the Deputy Archivist holds the second, and the Keeper of the Concord holds the third.

results.input: The old books say teleportation costs 30 mana. Can Aria Voss teleport out of the Ice Citadel with the mana she has?
results.answer:
No, Aria cannot teleport out of the Ice Citadel, and not because of mana.

The old books are outdated: teleportation actually costs 50 mana [57e9dcc6], and Aria has only 20 mana. But even if she had enough mana, the Citadel's four walls are warded against teleportation [1fe24429]. She cannot teleport out except during the Night of Thaw, when the eastern wall is unwarded for one night each year [c8557954].

[search_lore] passage 57e9dcc6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Teleportation): Teleportation costs 50 mana and cannot cross warded walls. The caster names a destination within one league (about five kilometres) and arrives there at once. A caster can carry only what they can carry on their own body. A teleporting caster cannot take another person with them.

Teleportation fails if the straight line to the destination crosses a warded wall, in either direction. A caster can teleport out of a warded place only if the path out does not cross a ward, which in practice almost never happens.

results.input: It is the Night of Thaw. Can Aria Voss teleport out of the Ice Citadel through the eastern wall?
results.answer: You're right. Aria cannot teleport out of the Ice Citadel through the eastern wall because she has only 20 mana, and teleportation costs 50 mana [57e9dcc6]. Although the eastern wall's ward is down on the Night of Thaw and can be crossed by teleportation [c8557954], Aria lacks the mana to cast the spell.
evidence: [fetch_character_state] Aria Voss is at Ice Citadel, condition healthy, mana 20, health 85, carries: flint, broken sword, health potion

[search_lore] passage 57e9dcc6 (The Magic of Aethel > Casting Rules > Teleportation): Teleportation costs 50 mana and cannot cross warded walls. The caster names a destination within one league (about five kilometres) and arrives there at once. A caster can carry only what they can carry on their own body. A teleporting caster cannot take another person with them.

Teleportation fails if the straight line to the destination crosses a warded wall, in either direction. A caster can teleport out of a warded place only if the path out does not cross a ward, which in practice almost never happens.
[search_lore] passage 4fded009 (The Magic of Aethel > Old Figures): Many old books give the price of teleportation as 30 mana. That was the price before the Sundering, when mana lay close to the surface of the world. The figure of 30 mana is out of date. The price today is 50 mana.
[search_lore] passage 010e67cb (Ember Keep > Rules of the Keep > The Keep has no wards): Ember Keep has never been warded. The Ember Court holds that walls are for those who are afraid of their neighbours, and has refused every offer of a ward. A caster can therefore teleport into the Keep, or out of it, for the normal price of 50 mana.

[search_lore] passage c8557954 (The Ice Citadel > The Wards > The Night of Thaw): Once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall of the Citadel is unwarded. The ward on the eastern wall goes down at midnight and comes back up at dawn. The Wardens say that the ice must be allowed to breathe while the Frost Binding renews itself.

During the Night of Thaw the eastern wall can be crossed by teleportation like any open ground, and the guard on the Eastern Postern is doubled. The other three walls stay warded. The Frost Binding that smothers fire magic stays in force all night, so fire magic is still impossible inside the Citadel on the Night of Thaw unless the caster possesses flint.
[search_lore] passage 1fe24429 (The Ice Citadel > Layout > The four walls): The Citadel has four walls: north, south, east and west. All four are warded. A warded wall cannot be crossed by teleportation, in either direction, so nobody can teleport into the Citadel or out of it. The western wall holds the Gate of Frost, which is the main entrance. The eastern wall holds a small door called the Eastern Postern, which is kept barred and guarded all year.
[search_lore] passage 7df66575 (The Ice Citadel > Overview): The Ice Citadel stands on the Northern Reach, on a spur of black rock above a frozen sea. Its walls are cut from blue glacial ice and set on foundations of dark stone. About eight hundred people live there, most of them Frost Wardens, their families and the servants who keep the Citadel running. It is the seat of the Frost Wardens and the coldest inhabited place in Aethel.

The Citadel is reached by the Gate of Frost in the western wall. The winter lasts nine months, and the Long Winter, the hardest forty days of the year, closes every road to the Citadel except the Ash Road to the south, which is usually passable.

results.input: Who can lower the wards of the Ice Citadel, and for how long?
results.answer: Only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal of the Frost Wardens, and only for one hour at a time [f34602a1]. There is also an exception: once a year on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern wall's ward drops automatically at midnight and stays down until dawn (the Night of Thaw), allowing teleportation through that wall [c8557954].

judge.reasoning: The answer says only the Warden-General can lower a ward, with the seal, for one hour at a time; passage f34602a1 states exactly this. It adds the Night of Thaw: once a year, on the last night of the Long Winter, the eastern ward goes down at midnight and comes back at dawn, and teleportation is possible through that wall. Passage c8557954 supports all of this. The word 'automatically' is a slight inference, but it fits the passage, so I treat it as supported. Every claim is backed by the evidence. results.input: Can Mira Sol cast fire magic while she is in Salt Harbour? Does she need flint?
results.answer:
Yes, Mira Sol can cast fire magic in Salt Harbour. She does not need flint. Fire magic can be cast anywhere in Nox without any special object, and flint has no meaning for magic in Nox [1c9fa262]. The only restriction is that fire magic is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine.

Mira Sol has 100 mana, so she has the resources to cast.

[search_lore] passage 4add25e6 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Tide Wards): The harbour walls are warded. The wards are called the Tide Wards, and they block teleportation in either direction. They are lowered for one hour at every full moon so that ships' crews can teleport their cargo ashore. During that hour a caster can teleport across the harbour walls for the normal price of 80 mana, without a Tide-key.
[search_lore] passage eb279661 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour): Salt Harbour is the great port of Nox, a city of white stone and tall masts on a bay of green water. About twelve thousand people live there. It is ruled by the Harbour Council, a body of nine ship-captains, and it is the only place in Nox where Tide-keys are issued.
[search_lore] passage 15f296c1 (Places of Nox > Salt Harbour > The Council House): The Council House stands on the quay. It is the only building in Nox that keeps a register of every Tide-key. A lost Tide-key must be reported within a day, and a replacement costs a month's wages.

[search_lore] passage 1c9fa262 (The Magic of Nox > Casting Rules > Fire magic): Fire magic can be cast anywhere in Nox without any special object, with one exception: it is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine, where the air holds firedamp that burns. Flint has no meaning for magic in Nox.
[search_lore] passage 8db439a2 (Places of Nox > The Hollow Mine > Fire in the Hollow Mine): Fire magic of any kind is forbidden inside the Hollow Mine, because the air holds firedamp. Open flames are forbidden too. Miners use sealed lanterns, which are lit with a spark from outside the mine. A caster who casts a fire spell inside the mine is expelled and fined.
